# Public forms

A form that creates a record for people without an account, such as a contact form, at its own address, behind a rate limit and a bot check.

A public form creates a record of a resource for anyone, signed in or not: a contact form, a quote request, a sign-up for an event. `.form(...)` on the resource's view declares it, and the [anonymous role](access.md#anonymous-access)) grants `create` of its fields. Visitors never read the records back, and the form is the only way an anonymous caller creates.

```ts title="config/contact_requests.ts"
import { f, resource, view } from '@protobase/schema'

// A shop's contact form: anyone, signed in or not, sends a request at /-/forms/contact; staff answer them in the app.

/** contact_requests */
export const contactRequests = resource('contact_requests')
  .table('contact_requests')
  .fields({
    id: f.integer().readOnly().filterable().sortable(),
    name: f.text().max(100),
    email: f.text().max(200),
    topic: f.enum(['order', 'repair', 'other']).default('other'),
    message: f.text().max(4000),
    handled: f.boolean().default(false).filterable(),
    created_at: f.timestamp().readOnly().sortable(),
  })
  .primaryKey((r) => r.id)
  .validate((request) => (request.email.includes('@') ? undefined : [{ field: 'email', message: 'Enter an email address' }]))
  // contact_requests.created: a job emails the shop about each one (see notify.ts)
  .events((e) => [e.created()])

export const contactRequestsView = view<typeof contactRequests>('contact_requests')
  .names({ singular: 'Contact request', plural: 'Contact requests' })
  .fields((r) => ({ name: r.name.label('Your name'), topic: r.topic.valueLabels({ order: 'An order', repair: 'A repair', other: 'Something else' }), message: r.message.multiline() }))
  .list((r) => ({ columns: [r.created_at, r.name, r.topic, r.handled], sort: [[r.created_at, 'desc']] }))
  .form((r) => ({
    name: 'contact',
    title: 'Contact us',
    fields: [r.name, r.email, r.topic, r.message],
    thanks: 'Thanks, we will reply within a day.',
  }))
```

```ts title="config/roles.ts"
import { defineRoles } from '@protobase/schema'

export const roles = defineRoles<'contact_requests'>({
  admin: ['*'],
  // Visitors create a contact request through the form, with these fields only, and never read one back
  anonymous: [{ 'contact_requests.create': ['name', 'email', 'topic', 'message'] }],
})
```

`.form({ name, fields, thanks, title?, perMinute? })` takes:

| | |
| --- | --- |
| `name` | Its address, `/-/forms/<name>`: lowercase letters, digits, `-` and `_`, unique across the app. |
| `fields` | The fields a visitor fills in, in order. |
| `thanks` | What the page shows once the form is sent. |
| `title` | The page's heading; the view's singular name by default. |
| `perMinute` | How many submissions one client may send per minute; 5 by default. |

Each call adds a form, so a view can have several.

## What the visitor sees

`/-/forms/<name>` in the admin app shows the form's title over a card with its fields, labelled, with their help and checks as the view gives them, and a **Send** button. It needs no sign-in and opens the same for someone who is signed in; link to it from your website. On **Send** the browser solves the bot check, about a second of work, then sends the form; the card then shows the `thanks` text. A field the server refuses shows its problem under the field, and any other refusal, such as too many submissions, shows above the button with what was typed kept.

## What a form accepts

A form takes plain fields: text, numbers, booleans, dates, enums, currencies and countries. The server refuses to start on a form with:

- a relation, since a visitor cannot read the records to pick one;
- a file field, since a visitor cannot upload;
- a sensitive, read-only or generated field;
- a field the anonymous role's `<resource>.create` does not list; the error names the entry to add;
- a field the resource does not have, or two forms of the same name;
- a field every create must give left out, since no submission could then be saved.

## The record

A submission is a create like any other, made by the anonymous role and limited to the form's fields: the resource's `.validate()` rules, record rules and write hooks run, and [events](events.md)), [webhooks](webhooks.md)) and [history](history.md)) see it. History names its maker **Visitor**.

### Email me on a new submission

There is no mail built into forms: the record's `created` event enqueues a [job](jobs.md)), and the job [sends the mail](jobs.md#mail)).

```ts title="config/notify.ts"
import { defineJob, FatalJobError, subscription } from '@protobase/server'
import { z } from 'zod'

// Email me on a new submission: the record's event enqueues a job, and the job sends the mail.

export const emailContactRequest = defineJob({
  name: 'email-contact-request',
  payload: z.object({ id: z.number() }),
  run: async ({ id }, { db, mail }) => {
    if (!mail) throw new FatalJobError('Mail is off: set PROTOBASE_SMTP_URL and PROTOBASE_MAIL_FROM')
    const request = await db.selectFrom('contact_requests').select(['name', 'email', 'message']).where('id', '=', id).executeTakeFirst()
    if (!request) return
    await mail.send({ to: 'shop@example.com', subject: `Contact request from ${request.name}`, text: `${request.email} wrote:\n\n${request.message}` })
  },
})

export const newContactRequests = subscription('newContactRequests', {
  events: ['contact_requests.created'],
  run: async (event, { db }) => {
    await emailContactRequest.enqueue(db, { id: Number(event.data.key) }, { key: `contact-request:${event.data.key}` })
  },
})
```

## Rate limit

Each client may send a form `perMinute` times a minute, 5 by default, as many as it may try to sign in. Past that, the form answers `429` with `Retry-After`. A client is known by its address in `X-Forwarded-For`, read as the sign-in limit reads it: a header with one address, an IPv6 address by its /64. Requests without one, or with several addresses, as a proxy makes when it appends to a header the client sent, share a single limit. The count is kept in each server process's memory, so with several instances each counts on its own, and a restart starts over.

## Bot check

Every submission carries a solved proof-of-work challenge ([ALTCHA](https://altcha.org)): the browser fetches a fresh one when the visitor presses **Send** and counts SHA-256 hashes until it finds the one the challenge asks for, about a second on a current laptop. There is no third-party service, cookie or visible puzzle, and it works offline. Sending many forms costs a bot that second each time, on top of the rate limit.

A challenge is made for one form, expires after 5 minutes and verifies once. The server signs challenges with `PROTOBASE_FORMS_SECRET`, or `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` when it is not set, and does not start with a form and neither variable, so give every instance of an app the same one. The browser solves the check with Web Crypto, which needs `https` or `localhost`.

## Routes

The form's page reads and sends it through three routes beside the API, which need no token:

| Route | |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/forms/<name>` | `{ name, title?, fields, thanks, resource, view }`: the resource restricted to the form's fields and the view's hints for them, as `/api/meta` gives them; `404` for a form that does not exist. |
| `GET /api/forms/<name>:challenge` | A fresh bot check. |
| `POST /api/forms/<name>` | `{ values, proof: { challenge, solution } }` creates the record: `204`, or the `400` with field errors a create answers; `400` `bot-check-failed` for a missing, wrong, expired or used check; `429` `too-many-submissions`. |

From code, [`@protobase/client`](client.md)) has `form(name)`, `formChallenge(name)` and `submitForm(name, values, proof)`; solve the challenge with `solveChallenge` from `altcha-lib`, as the page does.
